descricao_original: The principal fibers of the periodontal ligament secure the tooth in the socket and consist of five major subgroups: alveolar crest, horizontal, oblique, apical, and interradicular fibers, on multi-root teeth. These collagen fibers connect the cementum to the alveolar bone and grouped according to the regions they connect. Three of the five groups are visible in these images. 100x
creditos_identificados: Image source: These images were taken of a slide from the University of Michigan slide collection.

marcadores.explicacao_original: The alveolar crest is the uppermost part of the alveolar process. It forms a ridge of bone that surrounds the tooth at the level of the cementoenamel junction.

marcadores.explicacao_original: The oblique principal fibers are the most numerous fibers in the periodontal ligament. They connect the cementum along the remaining length of the root to the alveolar bone proper. These fibers provide the majority of support against the forces of mastication.
